question: How many independent, identical, successfully prepared trials give at least a 99% chance of a 122.06 keV photon emitted within 12 ns and eventually truly registered in the BART full-energy peak, at nominal calibration and throughout the declared endpoint box?

facts.preparation: One ordinary electronically occupied iron-57 nucleus successfully prepared at time zero in the 136.47 keV (5/2-) level, with no later driving or feeding. Calibration transfer uses an orientation-averaged emission ensemble with matched source placement, attenuation, and live acquisition.
facts.event: Emission of the 122.06 keV photon to the 14.4 keV level within 12 ns of preparation, followed by eventual full-energy-peak registration of that same photon in matched live acquisition.

measuredPopulationHalfLife.location: Bergmann, Javora and Smolyanskiy (2025), section 4, equation (6), 136.5 keV level
measuredPopulationHalfLife.conversion: The mean lifetime and its uncertainty equal the respective population half-life quantities divided by ln(2).

evaluatedPhotonWeights.location: DDEP comments, Table 5, Adopted column. The relative scale fixes gamma(2,1) at 100.

evaluatedTotalInternalConversionCoeffici.location: DDEP evaluated table, section 2.2, gamma(2,1) and gamma(2,0), alpha_T column.
evaluatedTotalInternalConversionCoeffici.definition: Total internal conversion rate divided by gamma emission rate for the same nuclear transition.

detector.name: BART
detector.geometry: Collins et al. (2015) BART geometry, 1 g aqueous standard in a 2 mL ISO ampoule at 30 cm perpendicular distance from the detector window, with water-normalized attenuation.

publishedCalibration.location: Collins et al. (2015), section 2.3.1, equation (1) and Table 3, 122.06 keV row

calibrationBox.source: Central values plus or minus each reported uncertainty in the Bergmann et al. equation (6), DDEP Comments Table 5 and evaluated section 2.2, and Collins et al. Table 3 inputs above. The bounds on conversion weights are the products of the corresponding photon-weight and conversion-coefficient endpoints. This is a declared sensitivity range for a calibration fixed across the run.
